lean.statement:
anonymous_statement : ∀
  {E : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup E] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℝ E] [inst_2 : FiniteDimensional ℝ E]
  [inst_3 : MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E] (P : MeasureTheory.Measure (E × ℝ))
  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure P],
  MeasureTheory.Measure.map Prod.fst P = ProbabilityTheory.stdGaussian E →
    ∀ (p : Polynomial ℝ),
      MeasureTheory.MemLp (fun z => z.2) 2 P →
        let S := { w // ‖w‖ = 1 };
        have V := fun ρ w =>
          2 *
            ∫ (z : E × ℝ),
              (∫ (v : S), Polynomial.eval (Inner.inner ℝ (↑v) z.1) p ∂ρ - z.2) *
                Polynomial.eval (Inner.inner ℝ w z.1) p ∂P;
        (∀ (ρ : MeasureTheory.Measure S), MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure ρ → ContDiff ℝ (↑⊤) (V ρ)) ∧
          ∀ (R : ℝ) (n : ℕ),
            ∃ C,
              0 ≤ C ∧
                ∀ (ρ : MeasureTheory.Measure S),
                  MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure ρ → ∀ (w : E), ‖w‖ ≤ R → ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ n (V ρ) w‖ ≤ C
approved_definition_context: All typeclasses and operators in the printed statement are standard Mathlib objects. The real inner product is literal Inner.inner R; the subtype S carries its induced Borel sigma algebra. stdGaussian E is the standard Gaussian probability on the finite-dimensional real inner-product space E. MemLp f 2 P means square integrability. The integral notation denotes the Bochner integral with Mathlib total semantics, returning zero when integrability fails; notation alone must not be read as a new integrability hypothesis or assertion.

The displayed smoothness order ContDiff R (up-arrow top) uses the coercion of the top of ENat into the extended smoothness-order type ENatOmega. It denotes C-infinity, not the analytic top order omega. iteratedFDeriv R n is the total n-fold Frechet derivative as a continuous multilinear map; at order zero its norm equals the norm of the function value. Its norm for positive orders is the multilinear operator norm. The definition of V and every dependence on the sphere measure are printed literally.
